I now have a complete picture. --- # Django + HTMX RealWorld Project — Structure & "User Blocking" Implementation Guide ## 1. Overall Directory / App Layout The project is a standard Django project with three local apps under `apps/`, plus shared `helpers/`, `config/` (project settings/urls), `templates/` (project-level, non-app), and a separate Playwright/e2e harness. ``` /home/claude/bench-ws/user-blocking-a-2/ ├── manage.py ├── Makefile # test/run/lint targets (see §6) ├── config/ # Django project package │ ├── settings.py # INSTALLED_APPS, AUTH_USER_MODEL="accounts.User" │ ├── urls.py # includes articles/accounts/comments urls │ ├── asgi.py, wsgi.py ├── apps/ │ ├── accounts/ # User model, auth, profiles, follow ← MOST RELEVANT │ │ ├── models.py, views.py, urls.py, forms.py, admin.py │ │ ├── migrations/ (0001..0003) │ │ └── management/commands/createUser.py │ ├── articles/ # Article model + feeds │ │ ├── models.py, views.py, urls.py, forms.py │ │ ├── migrations/ (0001..0003) │ │ ├── templatetags/markdown_filter.py │ │ └── management/commands/seed_data.py │ └── comments/ # Comment model │ ├── models.py, views.py, urls.py │ └── migrations/ (0001..0002) ├── helpers/ # htmx.py, exceptions.py, context_processors.py, tests.py ├── templates/ # base.html + accounts/ articles/ partials/ ├── static/ # css, images ├── playwright/ # playwright.config.ts └── realworld/specs/e2e/ # shared RealWorld Playwright specs + helpers ``` - `INSTALLED_APPS` registers the apps as `apps.accounts`, `apps.articles`, `apps.comments` (`config/settings.py:40-43`). Note: apps are imported without the `apps.` prefix inside code (e.g. `from accounts import views`), so `apps/` is on the path. - `AUTH_USER_MODEL = "accounts.User"` (`config/settings.py:143`). - Root URL routing (`config/urls.py:29-33`): all three app urlconfs are included at root `""`. ## 2. User/Profile Model & the "follow" Relationship There is no separate Profile model — the custom `User` (subclass of `AbstractUser`) holds profile fields (`bio`, `image`) and the follow relationship. **Follow is a self-referential, non-symmetrical `ManyToManyField` named `followers`.** `apps/accounts/models.py:29-54`: ```python class User(AbstractUser): first_name = None last_name = None email = models.EmailField("Email Address", unique=True) username = models.CharField(max_length=60, unique=True) bio = models.TextField(blank=True) image = models.URLField(null=True, blank=True) followers = models.ManyToManyField("self", blank=True, symmetrical=False) EMAIL_FIELD = "email" USERNAME_FIELD = "email" REQUIRED_FIELDS: list[str] = [] objects = UserManager() def get_full_name(self) -> str: return self.username def get_short_name(self) -> str: return self.username def is_following(self, other_user: User) -> bool: return other_user.followers.filter(pk=self.id).exists() if self.is_authenticated else False ``` Key semantics to understand for blocking: - `followers` is `symmetrical=False` on `"self"`. Because there is no `related_name`, the **reverse accessor is the auto-generated `user_set`**. In practice, the code treats it as: "the users in `X.followers` are the people who follow X." E.g. in `follow_view`, `profile_user.followers.add(request.user)` means request.user now follows profile_user. And `is_following(other)` checks `other.followers.filter(pk=self.id)`. - `UserManager` (`apps/accounts/models.py:7-26`) is a custom email-based manager. Migrations for the field: `followers` was created in the initial migration `apps/accounts/migrations/0001_initial.py:54` (`models.ManyToManyField(blank=True, to=settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL)`). Later migrations only rename `name`→`username` (0002) and alter `username` uniqueness (0003). **Latest accounts migration = `0003_alter_user_username.py`** (see §7). ## 3. Follow / Unfollow End-to-End **URL** — `apps/accounts/urls.py:12`: ```python path("profile//follow", views.follow_view, name="follow"), ``` **View** — `apps/accounts/views.py:129-151` (POST-only, login-required, toggles follow, returns HTMX partial or redirects): ```python @login_required @require_POST def follow_view(request, username): profile_user = get_object_or_404(User, username=username) if profile_user != request.user: if profile_user.followers.filter(pk=request.user.id).exists(): profile_user.followers.remove(request.user) is_following = False else: profile_user.followers.add(request.user) is_following = True else: is_following = False if is_htmx(request): return render(request, "partials/follow_button.html", {"profile_user": profile_user, "is_following": is_following}) return redirect("profile", username=username) ``` **Template partial** — `templates/partials/follow_button.html:1-7` (HTMX `hx-post`, self-replacing with `hx-swap="outerHTML"`): ```django {% if user.is_authenticated and user != profile_user %} {% endif %} ``` The follow button is rendered in two places: - Profile page: `templates/accounts/profile.html:18` (`{% include "partials/follow_button.html" %}`, else-branch of `is_self`). - Article meta (detail + used on article pages): `templates/partials/article_meta.html:20-22` — `{% include "partials/follow_button.html" with profile_user=article.author %}`. `article_meta.html` is what article `detail.html` renders for author follow. `is_htmx` helper — `helpers/htmx.py:4-5`: checks `HX-Request` header. ## 4. Where Profiles Are Displayed + Settings/Management Pages **Profile views** — `apps/accounts/views.py:81-126`. A shared `_profile_view(request, username, *, tab)` renders `accounts/profile.html`, with two thin wrappers: - `profile_view` (tab="my") → `apps/accounts/views.py:121-122` - `profile_favorites_view` (tab="favorites") → `apps/accounts/views.py:125-126` It computes `is_self` (line 93) and `is_following` (line 94), and filters articles by author or by `favorites=profile_user`. A missing user renders `accounts/profile_404.html` with 404 (lines 84-85). **Profile URLs** — `apps/accounts/urls.py:10-12`: ```python path("profile/", views.profile_view, name="profile"), path("profile//favorites", views.profile_favorites_view, name="profile_favorites"), path("profile//follow", views.follow_view, name="follow"), ``` **Profile template** — `templates/accounts/profile.html` (avatar/bio at top; `is_self` shows "Edit Profile Settings" link, else follow button at line 18; tabs "My Articles"/"Favorited Articles" via HTMX `hx-get` + `hx-select=".profile-page"`). **Settings page (the natural home for "manage blocked list")**: - View: `apps/accounts/views.py:57-72` (`settings_view`, login-required; `SettingsForm`). - Form: `apps/accounts/forms.py:20-34` (`SettingsForm(ModelForm)`, fields `image, username, bio, email` + password). - Template: `templates/accounts/settings.html` (single form + logout form). This is where a "Blocked Users" management section/list would fit. - URL: `apps/accounts/urls.py:8` (`path("settings", views.settings_view, name="settings")`). - Nav link to settings/profile: `templates/partials/header.html:15-25`. ## 5. Feeds & Where a User's Content Is Shown to Others **Feed logic** — `apps/articles/views.py:17-64` `_build_feed`. The "Your Feed" (following) branch is the key spot blocking must also affect: `apps/articles/views.py:28-38`: ```python if feed == "following" and not request.user.is_authenticated: return redirect("login") if feed == "following" and request.user.is_authenticated: followed_authors = User.objects.filter(followers=request.user) queryset = queryset.filter(author__in=followed_authors) active_tab = "following" elif tag: queryset = queryset.filter(tags__name=tag) active_tab = "tag" else: active_tab = "global" ``` Note `User.objects.filter(followers=request.user)` = "authors who have request.user in their followers" = authors request.user follows. - `home_view` / `tag_view`: `apps/articles/views.py:62-68`. - Feed toggle template (Your Feed / Global Feed tabs): `templates/partials/feed_content.html:1-33`. - Article list rows (shown to everyone; links to author profile): `templates/partials/article_list.html:1-35` (author link at lines 5-11). **Article detail** — `apps/articles/views.py:71-91`: loads article, its comments (`article.comment_set...`), and `is_following` for the author (line 82); renders `articles/detail.html`. **Favorites** — model field `Article.favorites` (M2M to user) in `apps/articles/models.py:38`; `with_favorites` annotates `num_favorites`/`is_favorite` (`apps/articles/models.py:13-22`); toggle view `article_favorite_view` (`apps/articles/views.py:151-162`) + `partials/favorite_button.html`. Profile "Favorited" tab filters `favorites=profile_user` (`apps/accounts/views.py:96-97`). **Comments** — model `apps/comments/models.py:6-11` (FK author + article). Comment list shows author name/avatar linking to profile: `templates/partials/comment_list.html:8-12`. Create/delete views: `apps/comments/views.py:11-35` (delete allowed for comment author or article author, line 29). Places where "B's content is shown to A" (all need blocking filters to fully hide a blocker from the blocked, or vice-versa): global feed article list, following feed, tag feed, profile article/favorites tabs, article detail author + comments, and the follow button availability. ## 6. Existing Test Patterns **Unit tests (Django `TestCase`)** — only one file: `helpers/tests.py`. It is intentionally minimal; the docstring (lines 1-8) states views/forms/models/templates are validated by the e2e suite, and unit tests exist only for hard-to-browser logic. Representative example (`helpers/tests.py:18-24`): ```python class CleanIntegrityErrorTest(TestCase): def test_sqlite_unique_violation(self): cause = SQLiteIntegrityError("UNIQUE constraint failed: accounts_user.email") error = IntegrityError(); error.__cause__ = cause self.assertEqual(clean_integrity_error(error), "email") ``` Run via Makefile: `make test-django` (`DEBUG=True ... manage.py test apps helpers`) or `make test-django-fast` (in-memory sqlite + fast hasher). There are currently **no app-level `tests.py`** in accounts/articles/comments — you'd add `apps/accounts/tests.py` following this `django.test.TestCase` pattern for blocking logic. **Playwright e2e tests** — in `realworld/specs/e2e/*.spec.ts`, with shared helpers in `realworld/specs/e2e/helpers/`. The most relevant is `social.spec.ts` (follow/unfollow, profiles, feeds). Representative example (`realworld/specs/e2e/social.spec.ts:22-43`): ```ts test('should follow and unfollow a user', async ({ page, request, browser }) => { const user = generateUniqueUser(); await register(page, user.username, user.email, user.password); let targetUsername: string; if (API_MODE) { targetUsername = 'johndoe'; } else { const otherUser = generateUniqueUser(); await createUserInIsolation(browser, otherUser); targetUsername = otherUser.username; } await followUser(page, targetUsername); await expect(page.locator('button:has-text("Unfollow")')).toBeVisible(); await unfollowUser(page, targetUsername); await expect(page.locator('button:has-text("Follow")')).toBeVisible(); }); ``` Helpers used: `helpers/profile.ts` (`followUser`/`unfollowUser`/`updateProfile`, lines 4-64), `helpers/auth.ts`, `helpers/articles.ts`, `helpers/setup.ts`, `helpers/api.ts`, `helpers/config.ts` (`API_MODE`). Config: `playwright/playwright.config.ts` (testDir `../realworld/specs/e2e`, baseURL `http://localhost:8000`, `fullyParallel:false`, `workers:1`). Run via `make e2e` (`API_MODE=false ... bun playwright test`). Other specs: `articles`, `auth`, `comments`, `settings`, `navigation`, `xss-security`, etc. Selector reference lives at `realworld/specs/e2e/SELECTORS.md`. A new blocking feature would add a spec here (e.g. `blocking.spec.ts`) and likely helpers in `helpers/profile.ts`. ## 7. Migrations Layout & Latest Numbers Each app has a `migrations/` package: - **accounts** (`apps/accounts/migrations/`): `0001_initial.py`, `0002_rename_name_user_username.py`, `0003_alter_user_username.py` → **latest = 0003**. A blocking field (e.g. `blocked = ManyToManyField("self", symmetrical=False, related_name=...)`) would be `0004_...`. The M2M pattern to copy is the existing `followers` field created in `0001_initial.py:54`. - **articles** (`apps/articles/migrations/`): `0001_initial.py`, `0002_alter_article_updated.py`, `0003_alter_article_created.py` → latest = 0003. - **comments** (`apps/comments/migrations/`): `0001_initial.py`, `0002_alter_comment_created.py` → latest = 0002. --- ### Implementation pointers for "user blocking" - Add a self-referential M2M on `User` (mirror `followers` at `apps/accounts/models.py:39`), e.g. `blocked = models.ManyToManyField("self", symmetrical=False, blank=True, related_name="blocked_by")`, plus helper methods like `has_blocked(other)` / `is_blocked_by(other)` alongside `is_following` (`apps/accounts/models.py:53-54`). from __future__ import annotations

from django.contrib.auth.models import AbstractUser, BaseUserManager
from django.db import models


class UserManager(BaseUserManager):
    def create_user(self, email: str, password: str | None = None, **other_fields) -> User:
        user = User(email=email, **other_fields)
        if password:
            user.set_password(password)
        else:
            user.set_unusable_password()
        user.save()
        return user

    def create_superuser(self, email: str, password: str | None = None, **other_fields) -> User:
        other_fields.setdefault("is_staff", True)
        other_fields.setdefault("is_superuser", True)
        other_fields.setdefault("is_active", True)

        if other_fields.get("is_staff") is not True:
            raise ValueError("Superuser must be assigned to is_staff=True.")
        if other_fields.get("is_superuser") is not True:
            raise ValueError("Superuser must be assigned to is_superuser=True.")
        return self.create_user(email, password, **other_fields)


class User(AbstractUser):
    # remove default fields
    first_name = None
    last_name = None

    email = models.EmailField("Email Address", unique=True)
    username = models.CharField(max_length=60, unique=True)
    bio = models.TextField(blank=True)
    image = models.URLField(null=True, blank=True)

    followers = models.ManyToManyField("self", blank=True, symmetrical=False)
    blocked = models.ManyToManyField("self", blank=True, symmetrical=False, related_name="blocked_by")

    EMAIL_FIELD = "email"
    USERNAME_FIELD = "email"
    REQUIRED_FIELDS: list[str] = []

    objects = UserManager()

    def get_full_name(self) -> str:
        return self.username

    def get_short_name(self) -> str:
        return self.username

    def is_following(self, other_user: User) -> bool:
        return other_user.followers.filter(pk=self.id).exists() if self.is_authenticated else False
